name: @projexlight/db-runtime
summary: Postgres pool runtime for ProjexCloud — multi-pool client (admin / app / evidence / global-catalog / warehouse / vector / olap), transaction helpers, dataService abstraction every SDK uses. Routes queries to the right pool via sdk-pool-router; PgBouncer-compatible connection management.

hooks.name: initPool
hooks.description: Initialize the global pool pool — reads DATABASE_URL per logical pool.

hooks.name: getPool
hooks.description: Get the pg.Pool for a named logical pool (admin / app / etc).

hooks.name: withTransaction
hooks.description: Run a callback inside a SERIALIZABLE transaction with automatic retry on conflict.

hooks.name: dataService
hooks.description: Higher-level service abstraction — repo-style methods over a logical pool.

scenarios.title: Service boots the pool once at startup
scenarios.when_to_use: Every service startup — initPool reads env, opens connections, runs migrations.
scenarios.example_code:
import { initPool } from '@projexlight/db-runtime';
await initPool({ logical: 'app' });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Pool ready; subsequent getPool() calls return without re-initialization.

scenarios.title: Multi-statement write in a transaction
scenarios.when_to_use: SDK writing multiple related rows — wrap in withTransaction so partial failures roll back atomically.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Both rows commit or neither. Serialization conflicts retried automatically up to N times.

scenarios.title: Route audit writes to evidence pool, billing to admin pool
scenarios.when_to_use: Universal pattern — each SDK declares its pool placement; db-runtime + pool-router handle the routing.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Hot writes on one pool don't starve others. Connection limits per pool independently tuned.

compliance_posture.notes: Connection strings only via env (never hardcoded). Statement-timeout enforced per pool to prevent runaway queries. SSL required for all pools.
